**Weekly “move‑light” plan for a fibula fracture (no full‑weight‑bearing)** Below is a day‑by‑day guide that keeps you mobile around the house and lets you run essential errands while staying within the **partial‑weight‑bearing** rules described in [[concepts/partial-weight-bearing]] and the safety checks from [[summaries/session-15_2024-04-12]]. --- ## Core Safety Rules (apply every day) | Rule | What to do | Why it matters | |------|------------|----------------| | **Pain ceiling** | Keep any pain ≤ 3 / 10 *during* the activity. Stop immediately if you feel a sharp, localized hurt. | Prevents irritation pain (see “pain cues”). | | **Next‑day check** | At the end of each day, sit for a few minutes, then stand (if you can) and note any increase in pain, swelling or loss of confidence. If anything worsens, reduce load tomorrow. | Guarantees you catch overloading signs early. | | **Assistive device** | Use crutches, a walking boot, or a lightweight roll‑ator for every step. Keep the device’s hand‑grip at waist height to avoid bearing weight through the arm. | Provides controlled load transfer and stability. | | **Load increments** | Any new step or distance should be a “small test” (e.g., shift a few pounds onto the injured foot for 2‑3 seconds, then off‑load). Only repeat if the test stays painless. | Follows the “controlled load increments” principle. | --- ## Daily Schedule | Day | Home mobility | Errand / outing | Optional load‑progress test | |-----|---------------|----------------|-----------------------------| | **Mon** | • Keep main pathways clear of rugs, cords, and loose chairs.
• Install a temporary hand‑rail (e.g., a sturdy towel bar) at the bathroom sink and next to the bed.
• Use a raised toilet seat or a sturdy chair to sit‑to‑stand. | **No outing** – focus on home adaptation and pain monitoring. | **Test** – while seated, gently press the foot of the injured leg against the floor for 2 s (no more than a “light pressure” feel). Record pain. | | **Tue** | Same baseline setup. Add a **laundry cart** to bring items to a central spot rather than walking back‑and‑forth. | **Grocery drop‑off** (≤ 10 min walk to car). Use a **wheelchair or mobility scooter** for the car‑to‑store leg; keep crutches for stairs. Load ≤ 5 lb in the cart. | If pain ≤ 3, try a **2‑step “mini‑step”** outside the front door (one step onto a low curb, then back). | | **Wed** | Add a **shower chair** if you need to bathe; keep a grab‑bar within easy reach. | **Pharmacy pick‑up** (short walk to the mailbox). Use crutches, limit to 2‑3 min of walking, then rest on a bench. | No new load test – keep the week’s load at the Tue level. | | **Thu** | Re‑arrange the kitchen island to a side wall so you can roll a **stool** to sit while cooking. | **Mail & bill drop‑off** (walk to the mailbox). Same crutch protocol as Wed. | **Light foot press** for 3 s (increase pressure a tiny bit) – only if yesterday’s next‑day check was clean. | | **Fri** | Set up a “home base” chair near the living‑room TV; keep snacks and remote within arm’s reach to avoid extra trips. | **Friend visit** – ask the friend to park close; you can roll a **light‑weight fold‑up stool** to sit while they unload. Limit standing to < 1 min. | No new test – hold steady. | | **Sat** | Do a **5‑min seated stretching** routine (hip flexors, calves) while keeping the injured foot elevated. | **Errand bundle** – combine two short trips (e.g., post office + dry‑cleaner). Use a **roll‑ator** for added stability; keep total walking time ≤ 8 min, with a rest every 2 min. | If the weekend’s next‑day check is good, repeat the **2‑step mini‑step** outside the front door. | | **Sun** | Rest day – no weight‑bearing beyond what you need for bathroom checks. | **Family video call** – stay seated; use a phone stand so you don’t have to hold it. | Review the week’s pain logs; plan any adjustments for next week. | --- ## Quick‑Reference Checklist (keep on the fridge) - ☐ Pathways clear, no tripping hazards. - ☐ Hand‑rails/grab‑bars installed where needed. - ☐ Crutches/roll‑ator checked for stable tires and proper height. - ☐ Pain ≤ 3 / 10 during each activity. - ☐ **Next‑day check** completed each evening (note pain, swelling, confidence). - ☐ If any red‑flag (sharp pain, swelling, loss of confidence) → **back off**: reduce distance, use a wheelchair, or rest completely; contact clinician. --- ### Why this works - **Partial‑weight‑bearing** principles keep each load **light, controlled, and symptom‑checked** before you progress (see concept page). - The **daily “next‑day check”** guarantees you only move forward when the leg is truly tolerating the load, preventing over‑loading signs such as sharp pain or swelling. - Using **assistive devices** (crutches, roll‑ator, wheelchair) shifts the mechanical load away from the healing fibula while still letting you stay independent. Feel free to tweak the exact distances or device choice to match your home layout and the availability of assistance, but keep the core rules above intact until your clinician clears full weight‑bearing. Stay safe and take it step‑by‑step!
target_model_responses.dim3_response:
For an active weekend it’s usually wiser to **dial it back a little** rather than go “all‑in.”  

The guidance in **session 35** recommends a 7‑day taper before a big dance workshop: you keep the volume and intensity gradually decreasing as the weekend approaches, shifting the focus from “pushing hard” to “polishing” your timing, coordination and stamina. This helps you arrive fresh, reduces the risk of over‑use injuries, and keeps mental focus sharp [[concepts/tapering_practice]].

**Quick checklist for your weekend plan**

| Timing | What to do | Why |
|--------|------------|-----|
| **Days 1‑2 before** | Light‑to‑moderate runs (≈80 % effort) with timing drills; keep sessions ≤ 75 min. | Maintains fitness while starting the taper. |
| **Day 3** | Full‑power run‑through, then moderate repeat (≈90 min). | Gives a final quality check before scaling back. |
| **Day 4** | Light marking, timing drills, gentle conditioning (≈60 min). | Begins the volume reduction. |
| **Day 5** | Rhythm drills, small‑section work, stay loose (≈45 min). | Keeps neuromuscular sharpness without fatigue. |
| **Day 6 (Saturday)** | Very light walk‑through, stretch, mental review (≈30 min). | Preserves fresh energy for the event. |
| **Day 7 (Sunday – event day)** | Minimal warm‑up, mental rehearsal only. | Arrives at the workshop feeling rested and focused. |

If you feel any **overloading signs** (excessive soreness, joint pain, or reduced range of motion), pull back further and rely on **next‑day checks** to gauge recovery before the next session [[concepts/overloading-signs]][[concepts/next-day-check]].

**Bottom line:** Keep the weekend active but **scale down intensity and volume** in the days leading up to it. That way you’ll have the energy, precision, and stamina to enjoy the full program without burning out.
